- on battery: one wake per percent, about every 52 min

issues.title: HDMI 2.1: 4K60 with 10 bpc falls back to 8 bpc over TMDS instead of using FRL
issues.author: Mato
issues.description:
### Brief summary of the problem

With max bpc 10, 3840x2160@60 only gets 8 bpc (the AVR info screen shows 8 bit). At 4K100 and 4K120 the same settings give 10 bpc. So 10 bpc RGB at 4K50/60 is never possible over HDMI, even when source and sink support FRL.

issues.title: Navi10 (RX 5600 XT): GPU writes to system RAM below 4 GB run at about 34 MB/s (above 4 GB: >10 GB/s), causing desktop-wide stalls
issues.author: Josh Weingarden
issues.description:
## Summary

What is going on is that any GPU-initiated write of more than 512 bytes to a system-memory
page whose physical (= bus) address is below 4 GB is throttled to about 34 MB/s.
The same write to a page above 4 GB completes at more than 10 GB/s. Data is always
correct. GPU reads from the same low pages are fast.

In normal use this shows up as the whole desktop dropping to 1–2 fps: under memory
pressure, GTT/userptr pages get allocated from ZONE_DMA32, a readback (screen
capture, VNC, software-composited browser with WebGL) then takes 100–470 ms per
frame, and that single job blocks the gfx ring for every other client. The desktop
"freezing" then stopped when the task that was copying memory from the gpu to RAM was
closed.

This has been driving me crazy ever since I switched to Linux a few years ago,
and I finally have a fix that stops the bug. However, the fix is to not use
any memory at an address of 4GB or less, which makes 2.9 GB of my memory unusable.
Due to not having internal documentation, I am unable to look into the root cause
for what is exactly going on.

issues.author: André Costa
issues.description:
**Summary**

On an Acer Swift SF14-61T (AMD Ryzen AI 9 365 / Radeon 880M, DCN 3.5) running Fedora 45 (kernel 7.3.4-300.fc45.x86_64, GNOME 51.1 on Wayland), letting the compositor turn off the built-in eDP-1 display via DPMS idle timeout while on battery causes a complete system hard-lock when attempting to wake the screen. The display stays black and all keyboard/input events are dead while the power LED remains on, requiring a forced shutdown via the power button.

Testing `amdgpu.dcdebugmask` flags isolates the issue to the interaction between DCN 3.5 Idle Power States (IPS) and eDP Panel Replay / PSR during DPMS-off transitions:

issues.title: drm/amdkfd: Stale KFD queues after GPU reset can trigger cascading resets
issues.author: Daniel Huang
issues.description:
## Summary

KFD queue teardown appears unable to execute during GPU reset because of a reset-domain lock conflict:

* `amdgpu_device_gpu_recover()` holds `reset_domain->sem` for writing.
* `remove_queue_mes()` attempts `down_read_trylock()` on the same semaphore and immediately returns `-EIO`.
* As a result, pre-reset teardown never reaches MES. This was confirmed with kprobes across two independent hangs.

The more significant issue appears to be **incomplete post-reset queue recovery**. `kgd2kfd_post_reset()` resumes KFD without reconciling queues that could not be removed. These queues remain valid in KFD's bookkeeping but may no longer exist in firmware.

A subsequent queue operation, including implicit removal during process exit, can fail and invoke `kfd_hws_hang()`, triggering another GPU reset. In one reproduction, the GPU remained unusable until reboot.

This was discovered while investigating [ROCm/TheRock#8357](https://github.com/ROCm/TheRock/issues/8357) (gfx90c/HWS). The same locking mechanism was reproduced on gfx1103/MES.

## Test environment

| Component | Configuration |

| GPU | Radeon 780M (gfx1103, Phoenix) |
| CPU | Ryzen 7 7840U |
| OS | Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS |
| Kernel | 7.0.0-38-generic |

issues.author: Nameless Seed
issues.description:
## Summary

Under heavy VRAM pressure (a Vulkan game filling the 8 GB card), the GPU raises a gfxhub page fault from the CPG client — a _write_ to a page whose PTE is not valid (`PERMISSION_FAULTS: 0x5`, `MAPPING_ERROR: 0x0`) — in the address space of a process other than the game (Xorg, or a browser compositing on the same GPU). The gfx ring then times out, the per-ring reset fails, a BACO reset follows, VRAM is lost and the whole desktop session is killed. issues.title: [DCN401] Cursor stutters on Xorg with two displays: static CRTC enables idle optimizations, so each cursor update does DMUB idle exit/enter
issues.author: Cláudio Forain
issues.description:
## Brief summary of the problem:

With **two displays active** on Xorg, the mouse cursor visibly speeds up and slows down while the desktop is otherwise idle. Physical mouse movement is steady, but on-screen motion is uneven. It reproduces every time and is easy to see.

* **Single display** (`xrandr --output DisplayPort-1 --off`): smooth.
* **Any rendering activity** (a tiny GL loop): smooth.
* **Kernels:** 7.1.12, 7.2.x and 7.3.3 are affected. 7.1.5 is not, because it still had [a1fc7bf6677e](https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/torvalds/linux.git/commit/?id=a1fc7bf6677e) (“drm/amd/display: Restore 5s vbl offdelay for NV3x+ DGPUs”). That workaround was reverted by [f39283eab44f](https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/torvalds/linux.git/commit/?id=f39283eab44f), which reached stable in 7.1.6. Older kernels (6.18.x) were also affected.
* Disabling GFXOFF, forcing `power_dpm_force_performance_level=high`, and `amdgpu.dcdebugmask=0x800` (DC_DISABLE_IPS) do **not** help.

### Root cause (from ftrace + code reading)

Idle optimizations are HW-wide, but the ISM runs **per CRTC**. `dm_ism_commit_idle_optimization_state()` allows idle optimizations globally when `!vblank_enabled && dm->active_vblank_irq_count == 0`. It doesn’t check whether the **other CRTCs’ ISMs** are idle.

So the static display’s ISM reaches `OPTIMIZED_IDLE` and turns global idle on, while the cursor display is busy. Xorg’s legacy cursor moves hold no vblank reference, so nothing vetoes it.

issues.author: Luis Andres Sobrido Andrade
issues.description:
## Summary

Two problems, the first one being the main subject of this issue:

1. FRL link training never reaches rate 5 (4×10G) on this sink, because of an FLT_UPDATE timeout.
2. As a consequence, 4K120 needs DSC, and FRL+DSC flickers (likely #5934).

With native HDMI FRL enabled (`amdgpu.dcfeaturemask=0x402`), FRL link-cap verification against a Samsung 2020 TV (QE55Q82T) **always** fails at FRL rate 5 (4 lanes × 10 Gbps). The failure is the same every time: the sink acknowledges the rate and requests LTP patterns, then never sets `FLT_UPDATE` again before the \~200 ms FLT timer expires. The driver then falls back to rate 4 (4 × 8 Gbps), which trains successfully within about 50–70 ms.

Because rate 4 is slightly short of the bandwidth needed for CTA 3840x2160@120 RGB 8 bpc, the driver enables DSC for that mode. With DSC over FRL, the picture **flickers and shows intermittent interference** after a while. This looks like a **second, separate problem**: DSC is within the sink's advertised DSC/FRL caps and should be stable even on a rate-4 link (see #5934). This issue is mainly about the training failure. The DSC instability is noted here because the training failure is what makes DSC necessary on this sink. With DSC disabled (`amdgpu.dcdebugmask=0x4`), 4K120 falls back to TMDS YCbCr 4:2:0.

Title: Use-after-free write to freed dm_connector_state (update_hdcp) on DP hotplug; kernel BUG on linux-hardened

## Brief summary of the problem:

Power-cycling a DisplayPort monitor (off and on with its power button) corrupts a freed `kmalloc-512` object that was a `dm_connector_state`. Nothing but the fbdev console is running on the display; no compositor, no Xorg.

With `slab_debug=FZPU` the kernel reports `Poison overwritten`: exactly one byte at object offset 448 is `0x01` instead of `0x6b`. Expected: hotplug does not corrupt memory. Frequency: reproduced on every attempt (3 of 3) on two kernels, within two or three hotplug events.

issues.title: amdgpu: udev-worker hangs, kworker hang in amdgpu_vce_idle_work_handler
issues.author: Amit Gurdasani
issues.description:
## Brief summary of the problem:

On booting the packaged 6.19.8 and 6.19.11 Debian-packaged amd64 kernels on my desktop equipped with an AMD Radeon R9 270X (Curacao XT from 2013), there is a hang during early boot in the initramfs as systemd-udevd enumerates devices. This ends up timing out after \~100 seconds, and the system eventually boots up. systemd-udevd ends up in unkillable sleep (D state), something also evidenced by kernel messages indicating that the udev-worker task remains blocked. It appears the issue originates from the amdgpu driver (also evidenced in the kernel task blocked messages).

The system fails to reboot or shut down in this state, as systemd-udevd is in D state, and I generally have to reset the system using the reset button, use a long press on the ATX power button to power down, or use Magic SysRq to reboot the machine.

Booting with the kernel command line option amdgpu.runpm=0; or amdgpu.ppfeaturemask=0xfff73fff; or amdgpu.aspm=0; or pci=noats; made no difference, the hang and D state of systemd-udevd happened regardless.

None of this happens with the Debian stable kernel 6.12.74.

I checked, and the issue is present in the upstream Linux kernel as well. I was able to use git bisect to pinpoint the commit from which the issue is exhibited (between 6.18.0-rc2 and 6.18.0-rc3):

```
git bisect start
# status: waiting for both good and bad commits
# good: [7d0a66e4bb9081d75c82ec4957c50034cb0ea449] Linux 6.18
